clue.text: Raw talent given suit after part of course

indicators.note: the card suit is placed after the golf-course term, so it comes second

parts.note: the rough is the long grass bordering a golf fairway
diamonds is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone gifted but unpolished is handed a suit after a round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of natural ability who lacks polish is likened to an uncut gem, a common idiom.

clue.text: Irritates the French following row

indicators.note: the French article comes after the word for row, so it is written second

parts.note: a rank is a line or row, as of soldiers or taxis
les is the French plural word for the

explanation.surface: Being stuck behind the French in a queue gets on someone's nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to cause lasting resentment, a synonym of irritating someone.

clue.text: Music-maker from this country left to go into posh sheltered place

parts.note: for a British paper, this country is the UK
U is the crossword letter for upper-class, posh

indicators.note: signals that the letter for left is placed inside the word for shelter

parts.note: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind

explanation.surface: A British instrument is left lying in a smart, protected spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go into' puts L inside LEE between its two Es, giving LELE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small four-stringed guitar is an instrument, here loosely called a music-maker.

clue.text: Spare holy ground for boisterous activity

indicators.note: past tense of grind: the letters of the two words are crushed and reformed

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to leave a sacred site free of rowdy behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun paired with 'holy', but it is the anagram signal on SPAREHOLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough, high-spirited play is exactly what the term for this boisterous fooling describes.

clue.text: Old despot with empty outburst, thick type

parts.note: Idi Amin was the brutal ruler of Uganda in the 1970s

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outside letters, the middle being removed

explanation.surface: A former tyrant with a hollow rant is a stupid sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick means stupid in British slang, so a thick type is a fool.

clue.text: Wrongly term claims concocted by lecturer

indicators.note: concocted means made up, so the letters of claims are rearranged

explanation.surface: An academic invents claims and mislabels something.
explanation.definitionFit: To call something by the wrong name is to give it a wrong term.

clue.text: Third character in Lent in a poor condition holding fast

indicators.note: picks only the third letter of the following word

parts.note: ailing means unwell, in poor health

explanation.surface: During Lent someone sick is clinging on.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailing something fixes it firmly in place, as with nails, so it is holding fast.

clue.text: Part of pack mischievously hid can full of weight — and big snack

parts.note: clubs is one suit in a pack of playing cards

indicators.note: the anagram holds the letter for weight inside it
acting mischievously suggests the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Somebody naughtily hides a heavy tin as part of a pack before a large meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mischievously' scrambles the two words to ANDICH, and 'full of' puts W inside that to make ANDWICH; 'Part of pack' is the card suit, not a rucksack.
explanation.definitionFit: A multi-layered sandwich of several fillings is a substantial snack.

clue.text: A long run largely devised to produce weariness

indicators.note: devised means worked out afresh, so the letters are rearranged
most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A long jog, mostly planned, leads to exhaustion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts RUN to RU; A LONG RU is then rearranged by 'devised'.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is a state of listless tiredness, a synonym of weariness.

clue.text: Town is accommodating quiet jam makers by church

indicators.note: the word is holds the letter for quiet inside it

parts.note: taken as written
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
the WI, Women's Institute, is a British women's organisation famous for jam-making

explanation.surface: A town houses quiet jam makers next to a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipswich is the county town of Suffolk in eastern England.

clue.text: Fashion in judicial investigation producing much sorrow

indicators.note: the word for fashion sits inside the word for a court session

parts.note: a hearing is a court's examination of a case
a trend is a fashion or vogue

explanation.surface: A fashion craze turns up during a court case and causes great grief.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deeply distressing is said to wrench the heart, causing much sorrow.

clue.text: Hold first woman trailing bishop and priest

indicators.note: the first woman follows behind the others, so she comes last

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel
Eve is the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: Eve follows a bishop and a priest in a religious procession.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold an opinion is to believe it, a synonym in the sense of maintaining a view.

clue.text: Imperial figure from Amritsar in ashram

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A royal personage emerges from Amritsar in a religious retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife of a Russian emperor was an empress, an imperial figure.

clue.text: Dogs, perhaps, heard in part of supermarket

indicators.note: signals that the word must be said out loud to give the answer

parts.note: the Isle of Dogs is a district of East London, so Dogs is an example of an isle

explanation.surface: Dogs are heard barking in one part of a supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Dogs is a district of East London on a bend of the Thames; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage between shelves of goods in a shop is a walkway section of the store.

clue.text: Fib about male getting insubstantial public exposure?

indicators.note: the word for fib goes around the letter for male

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
light means flimsy, lacking weight

explanation.surface: A lie about a man gets flimsy press attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the full glare of public attention is the stage-lighting idiom for exposure.

clue.text: Preserve a dram with meal that's cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests the ingredients are mixed and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A preserve is made with a tot of whisky and some meal in the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: This citrus jam is a fruit preserve, usually made from oranges.

clue.text: Animals taken round second old city in ship

indicators.note: the word for animals is wrapped around the other pieces

parts.note: deer are animals
Troy is the ancient city of Homer's Iliad

explanation.surface: Animals are carried around an ancient city on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast warship escorting a fleet is a type of naval ship.

clue.text: American priest in religious group, one wanted by the police?

indicators.note: the American and priest letters sit inside the word for group

parts.note: a sect is a religious group

explanation.surface: An American priest belonging to a cult is being sought by police.
explanation.definitionFit: A person believed guilty of a crime is someone the police are looking for.

clue.text: Page put in memorial with a copy

indicators.note: the letter for page is placed inside the word for memorial

parts.note: a relic is something kept as a remembrance

explanation.surface: A page is placed in a memorial along with a copy.
explanation.definitionFit: An exact reproduction of something is a copy of it.

clue.text: Manage to follow shop's principal range

indicators.note: the word for manage comes after the selected letter
the principal, first, letter of the word is taken

parts.note: to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: A trainee manager is told to follow the shop's boss across the whole range.
explanation.definitionFit: Scope means the extent or range of something.

clue.text: Extend time inside

definitions.meaning: to lengthen or pull out further
a period spent in prison, British slang

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to pull something out longer and a jail sentence.

clue.text: Supervised position of carpenter at work?

definitions.meaning: a carpenter cutting wood stands above the tool

explanation.definitionFit: Watched over in a managing role, and read as two words a woodworker's stance above a tool.

clue.text: Popular drink I had in flat

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a sip is a small drink
contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: A popular drink I had was dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat in the sense of dull and lacking flavour is a synonym.

clue.text: Figure getting mine owner's instruction in pit?

definitions.meaning: a boss telling miners to excavate something

explanation.definitionFit: A numeral is a figure, and split into two words it is a command to excavate.

clue.text: Excellent teacher restraining troublemaker finally, vacant sort

indicators.note: the outer pieces hold the selected letter inside

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate
a head is a headteacher

indicators.note: takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A first-rate head teacher keeps a troublemaker in check, but is an empty-headed sort.
explanation.definitionFit: An empty-headed, foolish person is a vacant sort.

clue.text: Like one observant ambassador say hosting big noise

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: the abbreviation for example holds the word for noise inside it

parts.note: eg, for example, is signalled by say
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: An ambassador hosts a loud party and takes careful note.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying attention describes a watchful person, so it is how an observant one behaves.

clue.text: Skill is a necessity principally for mechanic

parts.note: art is skill or craft

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Skill is chiefly what a mechanic needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual worker is a craftsman, which is an old sense of mechanic.

clue.text: Hotel stew has to be replaced to attract the most publicity

indicators.note: the letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A hotel's stew has to be swapped, so it grabs the headlines.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from theatre: to outshine every other performer and draw most attention.
